title: Safe Overtaking of Water Trucks
body: DT operators are currently overtaking water trucks on corners, on gradient, with no radio call, and while the truck is still moving — stacking four SOP violations into one maneuver. That's the exact setup for a berm overrun or a high-wall contact on a switchback, not a hypothetical.
keyPoints: Radio the water truck operator first and get a "clear to pass" before overtaking — hearing you is not the same as confirming it's safe.
No overtaking on switchbacks or blind corners. Forward visibility drops mid-turn and the outside berm is the only thing stopping an overrun.
No overtaking on gradient. Uphill 40 km/h and downhill 30 km/h are ceilings — the speed differential on a ramp is exactly where sightline and braking distance are already worst.
Never overtake a vehicle that's still moving without that operator's confirmation. They may be turning into a spray pattern or reversing to top up and not see you coming.
Can't raise the bowser operator on radio? You don't overtake. Follow at distance or wait for them to pull over.
apply: Any overtake of a water truck today that skips the radio call, happens on a corner or ramp gradient, or passes a truck still in motion is a finding on the spot — and the same four stacked together again goes through as an LSR 6 (Mobile Equipment) matter.
